set.body:
Objective:
Implement Frame materialization as immutable Table[Schema] values composed of scoped Arrow-compatible record batches on JVM and Scala.js. Reuse the Arrow physical specification and platform implementations through adapters; do not build a competing general-purpose columnar format or production execution engine.

Required model:
- Separate logical DType, field nullability, physical encoding, and buffer layout.
- Primitive nulls use validity bitmaps; placeholder values in invalid slots have no meaning.
- Shared Buffer, ArrayData, RecordBatch, and Table contracts are platform-neutral. JVM ArrowBuf or optional FFM access and JavaScript ArrayBuffer or typed-array access live behind platform modules.
- Materialized batches and tables have explicit owned or borrowed lifetimes. Lazy Frame plans do not own open streams or buffers.
- Slicing may share buffers; mutation is confined to builders that cannot unsafely alias finished values.
- Arrow interoperability is layout- and lifetime-specific. Arrow-compatible does not imply that every ingestion, rechunk, join, or matrix conversion is zero-copy.

Initial types:
Boolean, Int32, an explicit cross-platform Int64 policy, Float32, Float64, UTF-8, timestamps, and dictionary encoding. Nested list and struct layouts may remain follow-on work if the first contracts leave a lawful extension seam.

Acceptance:
- RecordBatch and scoped batch-source contracts preserve schema and chunk boundaries, and Table[Schema] is visibly distinct from Frame[Schema].
- Required and nullable primitive arrays pass Arrow-layout fixtures, slicing laws, and scalar/vector access parity on JVM and JS.
- No primitive column store boxes Option or Any values internally.
- Ownership tests cover retained slices, borrowed inputs, deterministic close, leak accounting where available, structured use-after-close failure, early stream termination, and failed collection.
- The shared module contains no java.lang.foreign, Arrow Java, filesystem, Polars, DuckDB, ScalaFIM domain, or Gale types.
- Bench receipts cover scan, slice, validity traversal, and allocation behavior without unsupported zero-copy or production-engine claims.
